brief.t: Founded in December 2015 in Bengaluru by Sameer Nigam, Rahul Chari and Burzin Engineer; Flipkart bought it in 2016, and it separated from Flipkart in 2022 with Walmart as majority owner (about 72%).
It runs India's most-used UPI app: about 46% of UPI transactions by volume in mid-2026, ahead of Google Pay (about 32%), per NPCI data.
Payments are free for users, so it also earns from merchants (payment gateway, smart speakers), and by distributing loans, insurance and investments for partners.
FY 2025-26: revenue from operations ₹7,920 crore (+11.5%) and a net loss of ₹2,792 crore (up from ₹1,727 crore), driven mainly by ESOP (share-based pay) costs.

Not listed yet: SEBI cleared its IPO (an offer for sale by Walmart, Microsoft and Tiger Global) in Jan 2026, but it paused the IPO in Mar 2026 because of market volatility. Reports in Sep 2026 said it now aims to list around Feb–Mar 2027.

timeline.t: Founded in Bengaluru by Sameer Nigam, Rahul Chari and Burzin Engineer.
Acquired by Flipkart; Sameer Nigam became CEO.
Separation from Flipkart completed and domicile moved from Singapore to India; Walmart stays majority owner.
SEBI approval (after a confidential filing in Sep 2025); updated draft prospectus filed for an offer-for-sale-only IPO.
IPO paused, citing West Asia tensions and market volatility.
Share.Market renamed PhonePe Invest; Indus Appstore renamed PhonePe Appstore.

model.how: Sending money by UPI is free for users, and most small payments to shops are free too. PhonePe uses its huge user base to earn in other ways: fees from merchants and billers, rentals for smart speakers, advertising, and commissions for distributing loans (for banks and NBFCs), insurance and investments.
flow: Users pay and send money on UPI for free
Merchants pay for gateway services and devices
Data and trust help sell loans, insurance and investments
Earns fees and commissions, minus tech, staff and marketing costs

industry.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and NPCI (for UPI); SEBI for broking and IRDAI for insurance broking
points: UPI was zero-fee for merchants since 2020. In Sep 2026 the government announced a 0.4% fee (MDR) on some merchant payments above ₹2,000, with small merchants and person-to-person payments still free; the start was pushed to after Diwali.
NPCI plans to cap any app at 30% of UPI volume; the deadline for existing apps is 31 Dec 2026. PhonePe and Google Pay are each well above 30% today.
Big interview theme: how a payments app with free UPI turns its users into a profitable business.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Revenue: Total money earned from the business in a period, before costs.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.Market share: A company's sales as a % of the total sales of its industry.
glossary.Consolidated: Figures for the company together with its subsidiaries. 'Standalone' means the parent company alone.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account or selling a product.
glossary.UPI: Unified Payments Interface: India's instant bank-to-bank payment system run by NPCI. Apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm sit on top of it.
glossary.NPCI: National Payments Corporation of India: the body that runs UPI, RuPay and other retail payment systems.
glossary.MDR: Merchant Discount Rate: the fee a shop pays on each digital payment. UPI and RuPay debit card payments have zero MDR by government rule.
glossary.GMV: Gross Merchandise Value: the total value of payments that pass through a platform in a period.
glossary.Payment aggregator: A company licensed by RBI to collect online payments for merchants and pass the money to them.
glossary.Soundbox: A small speaker device at a shop that announces each payment received, for a monthly fee.
glossary.Contribution margin: Revenue minus direct costs (like payment processing). Shows if the core business makes money before fixed costs.
glossary.EBITDA: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation: a measure of operating profit.
glossary.Loan distribution: Helping a bank or NBFC give loans to customers and merchants for a fee, without lending its own money.
glossary.Market share cap: An NPCI limit (proposed at 30%) on how much of UPI transactions any one app can handle.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates payments, banks and NBFCs in India.
glossary.Fintech: Financial technology: companies that use apps and software to offer payments, loans, investing or insurance.
glossary.Net loss: When total costs are more than total income for the period. The opposite of net profit.
glossary.ESOP: Employee Stock Option Plan: shares or options given to staff as pay. Their cost is shown as an expense, even though no cash leaves the company.
glossary.DRHP: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: the first IPO document a company files with SEBI, with its business, risks and financials.
glossary.Offer for sale: An IPO where existing shareholders sell their shares. The company itself gets no new money.
glossary.Lending service provider: A company that finds borrowers for banks and NBFCs and helps service loans, without lending its own money.
glossary.SEBI: Securities and Exchange Board of India: the regulator of stock markets, IPOs and brokers.
glossary.P2M: Person-to-merchant: a UPI payment from a customer to a shop or business. P2P means person-to-person.

Finance.q: PhonePe's revenue grew in FY26 but its loss widened. Why?
Finance.a: Revenue from operations rose 11.5% to ₹7,920 crore, but expenses rose 16% to ₹10,589 crore. Most of the loss came from ESOP (share-based pay) costs, a non-cash expense, plus a one-time write-off.

Finance.q: What is an offer-for-sale IPO and who was selling in PhonePe's?
Finance.a: Existing shareholders sell shares and the company gets no new money. In PhonePe's draft, Walmart planned to sell part of its stake, and Microsoft and Tiger Global planned to exit fully.

Marketing.q: How would you get a PhonePe UPI user to try PhonePe Invest?
Marketing.a: Target users who already buy gold or mutual funds in the app, show simple goals (e.g. 'start a ₹500 SIP'), build trust with clear fees, and use in-app nudges at the right moment.

Marketing.q: Why did PhonePe rename Share.Market and Indus Appstore in Oct 2026?
Marketing.a: To bring them under the trusted PhonePe brand so its large user base recognises them, and to make cross-selling easier.

HR.q: PhonePe saw several senior exits in 2026. How would you retain key leaders?
HR.a: Clear growth paths, long-term rewards such as ESOPs, ownership of big projects, and strong internal promotions, like Srijon Biswas becoming CTO in July 2026.

Sales.q: Convince a kirana shop owner to take a PhonePe smart speaker.
Sales.a: It announces every payment aloud, so no need to check the phone or fear fake screenshots; fewer disputes and faster checkout during rush hours, for a small monthly fee.

Operations.q: How would you keep UPI payments working at over 1,000 crore transactions a month?
Operations.a: Strong tech uptime with backups, fast fraud checks, quick complaint resolution and close work with banks and NPCI on failed payments.

Other.q: What does the new UPI MDR mean for PhonePe?
Other.a: A 0.4% fee on merchant payments above ₹2,000 (small merchants and P2P stay free) could give UPI apps a direct income from payments for the first time. The rollout was moved to after Diwali 2026.

common.a: Co-founder Sameer Nigam is CEO; co-founder Rahul Chari is Chief Product and Technology Officer; Rohit Bhagat chairs the board. Walmart is the majority owner.

common.q: Is PhonePe listed on the stock market?
common.a: No. SEBI approved its IPO in Jan 2026, but it paused the IPO in Mar 2026 due to market volatility. Reports say it may list in early 2027.

interview.why_us: PhonePe handles almost half of India's UPI payments and is used by over 60 crore people, from big cities to small villages. It is now building loans, insurance and investing on top of payments, and preparing to go public. Working here means learning how a fintech serves India at huge scale and turns free payments into a business. I want to contribute to [your role] in this next stage.
ask: How will the new UPI MDR change PhonePe's merchant business?
Which financial services, such as PhonePe Invest or lending, are the biggest growth focus for the next two years?
What does success look like for a new joiner in the first six months?

gd.t: Should UPI payments to merchants carry a fee (MDR)?
gd.for: Apps and banks need income to keep UPI safe, reliable and growing; big merchants can afford a small fee.
gd.against: Fees may push small shops back to cash and slow down digital payments.

gd.t: Should any one UPI app be capped at 30% market share?
gd.for: Too much dependence on two apps is a risk to the system; caps encourage competition.
gd.against: Users choose apps freely; forcing limits punishes popular products and hurts user experience.

avoid: Don't say PhonePe is listed or quote a share price; its IPO is still pending.
Don't call PhonePe a bank or an NBFC lender; it distributes loans for banks and NBFCs.
Don't use old names without the update: Share.Market is now PhonePe Invest and Indus Appstore is now PhonePe Appstore (Oct 2026).
